headline: Lānaʻi commission hears update on inter-island internet cable

meeting.summary: The commission heard a presentation on a proposed undersea internet cable; no action was taken, and the next meeting is September 16.
meeting.recap: A new commissioner attended her first meeting.[[0:01:40]] A county planner said the presentation was for information only, with no action taken.[[0:17:41]] The presenter said a cable landing station building is no longer needed on Lānaʻi.[[0:21:14]] Construction is expected to take about a month.[[0:29:05]] The state historic preservation division asked for an archaeological survey with digging tests.[[0:32:29]] No one signed up to give public testimony.[[0:38:34]] A commissioner asked about digging near a harbor road that was once closed for years.[[0:39:24]] A team member said the cable now serving Lānaʻi is 29 years old.[[0:47:06]] A team member said there would be no cost to Lānaʻi residents.[[1:00:24]] Staff said a rule change for minor special management area (SMA) permits should be finished by next month's meeting.[[1:04:47]] The next meeting is September 16.[[1:07:49]] The chair asked that three commission seats opening March 31, 2027 be listed in the director's report.[[1:09:13]]
meeting.next: A future permit for the cable project will come before the commission for action. The rule change goes to the mayor and county clerk, and takes effect within 10 business days of the clerk receiving it. Next month's agenda includes County Council resolution 26-68, which would require notice to lessees when agricultural land is subdivided. The chair said he would look for information on a vacant county property a commissioner asked about and share it by email through staff. Staff agreed to find out where the Lānaʻi community plan stands in the county's review order.
